strategic_themes.title: ASC fee uplift modelling + provider risk mitigation
strategic_themes.rationale: ASC market sustainability concern: Council uplift offered is BELOW its own internal cost-pressure number. Council exposure to provider failure + Care Act s.18 statutory duty (must arrange care). Mitigation levers: (a) Cost of Care benchmark refresh, (b) blocked-bed pricing for high-needs cohorts, (c) jointly-commissioned frameworks with NHS ICB, (d) workforce strategy to reduce agency-cost dependency.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of Adult Social Care + Cabinet Member

strategic_themes.title: Norse Group LATCo VfM review (£350M/yr turnover)
strategic_themes.rationale: Norse Group is UK's largest LATCo (CN 05694657, 9,500 employees, c.£350M turnover). 6 trading subsidiaries beyond Norse Care: Norse Commercial Services, Norse Eastern, NPS Group, Norse Consulting, nplaw. £13.7M group loss 2021-22 due to property + goodwill impairment in Norse Consulting. Care-home contract restructure + sale to Stow Healthcare Group removes the loss-making contract; remaining 5 subsidiaries' VfM unchallenged. Standard LATCo VfM levers: (a) market-test each service line every 3-5 years, (b) FRS 102 s.33 related-party disclosure quality + arm's-length pricing, (c) cross-county trading competitive-neutrality (state-aid risk if subsidising bids into other authorities), (d) supply-chain payment performance (identified as one of UK worst-paying LATCos).

strategic_themes.title: Recover £28.5M Norse Care debt via care-home sale
strategic_themes.rationale: Norfolk-commissioned audit found Norse Care Ltd owes £28.5M to Norfolk County Council. Sale of 20 care homes to Stow Healthcare Group will apply sale proceeds to outstanding debt. One-off recovery — lock in proceeds during public consultation phase 16 Feb – 22 Mar 2026.

strategic_themes.title: Highways term-maintenance contract benchmarking (£700M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Highways term-maintenance contract: Kier. OPEN — fresh April 2026 baseline. Open-book pricing review, JCT-style PPM benchmarking, social-value measurement and rate-card comparison vs Crown Commercial Service framework rates standard. 3-7% saving on labour/materials/overhead lines typical from open-book in early-contract period.

strategic_themes.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£4M concentrated)
strategic_themes.rationale: £4M of agency-staff spend across 2 master vendors. Top: COMENSURA LTD (£2M), JMR RECRUITMENT LTD (£1M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of HR + Director of Finance + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£21M baseline)
strategic_themes.rationale: £21M utility spend across 3 suppliers. Top: TOTALENERGIES GAS & POWER LTD (£20M), THE LEONARD CHESHIRE FOUNDATION LTD (£1M), LEONARD CHESHIRE DISABILITY (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of Property + Sustainability Lead + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £1179M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Annual revenue £1474M implies indicative CFR c. £1179M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

strategic_themes.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative pay bill £590M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £130M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

strategic_themes.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£147M base)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £147M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

strategic_themes.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£1.5M premium estimate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £1.5M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

strategic_themes.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (88 notices; 3 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
strategic_themes.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 88 notices (27 awarded, £20M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 3 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £163M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: Life Opportunities for Adults in Norfolk - Lot 1 Learning Di (ceiling £95M); Framework for Home Support Providers for West & North No (ceiling £56M); Tranche 2 Type B Fire Appliances - AWARD (ceiling £12M). Matched against ledger: Tranche 2 Type B Fire Appliances - AWARD — ceiling £11.8M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.9M; Gas Monitoring Equipment for NFRS - AWARD — ceiling £0.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £19.6M; Framework for Home Support Providers for West &amp — ceiling £0.0M, actual ledger spend with awardee £19.1M. Aggregate identified actual spend £237M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Cabinet Member + Section 151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Companies House compliance follow-up (£59M flagged — 1 overdue, 1 dissolved, 1 insolvency-history)
strategic_themes.rationale: Companies House lookup on top-50 suppliers identified £59M of spend with statutory-compliance flags: £18M to suppliers with overdue accounts (1), £24M to dissolved-status companies (1), £18M to companies with insolvency history (1). NOTE: Some matches are CH fuzzy-search false positives (e.g. school, government-body name collisions) and need human verification. After verification, real flags = (a) credit-risk review on overdue accounts, (b) contract-cleanup on dissolved entities (records still on ledger but supplier extinct — risk of duplicate-payment leakage), (c) PCR 2015 Reg.57 discretionary exclusion review on insolvency-history suppliers in active contracts.

strategic_themes.title: Rebuild general reserves to ≥4 months (Critical → Adequate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Reserves at 2.4 months (Critical per CIPFA Resilience benchmark). Direction: stable. A 4-month minimum is the CIPFA / S151 prudence floor; below this triggers external auditor VFM concern and elevates s.114 risk.

strategic_themes.title: Audit + recover £106M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £106M across 14,786 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

strategic_themes.title: Investigate £674M in flagged split-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE flagged £674M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.
